ApiError.description: An error as the API carries it, in results and `last_error`.

oneOf.description: Audio when the source has it.
Video-first: audio m-lines answered `inactive`, no transcoder.

talker.description:
The session that held the backchannel when the command arrived, as
the worker last reported it; null when it was free. A
`talker_changed` with `released` follows on `stream/subscribe` when
one was released. A release conditional on a `session_id` reports
the talker the same way, whichever session it is: the worker frees
the backchannel only if that session still holds it when the
release arrives, so the `talker_changed` is what tells.

BackchannelState.description: Whether a session holds a source's backchannel.

oneOf.description:
Nobody talks and no camera session of it is open: the next offer

A session holds it, the stream's `backchannel.talker`: the

clients.description: Every allowed pin, ordered by pin.

ClipEvent.description:
An event of `clip/start`, in the order they come: `started` unless
the clip ends first, then warnings and gaps, and `stopped` always last.
Each variant's schema title names the Python client's class for it.

oneOf.description:
The clip's file is under way: its first bytes are on their way to

at.description:
When it started, RFC 3339 UTC: the daemon's time of the start,
which `before_ms` counts back from.

audio.description:
Its audio; null for a clip without audio (`audio: false`, a
stream without audio, or `audio_omitted`).

before_ms.description:
How far before `at` the clip begins, in milliseconds: the age
of the keyframe it starts at, which is what the pre-roll window
held, not what was asked; 0 without a window.

oneOf.title: ClipEventWarning

oneOf.description:
The clip has a hole: no media between `from_ms` and `to_ms`, so

Where the hole begins, in milliseconds of the clip's media time

The last event; the subscription ends with it, and the body ends

bytes.description:
The bytes of the file written to the body; 0 when the clip
ended without its worker's last word (`worker_crashed`,
`stream_deleted`, `stream_changed` by a move to another

duration_ms.description:
The media time the file covers, in milliseconds; 0 for the

gaps.description:
The gaps the clip had, every one counted even where not each

ClipGapReason.description: Why a clip has a hole: the `reason` of `gap`.

oneOf.description:
The camera's connection dropped and came back, during the clip or

Video frames are missing inside one connection: two consecutive
ones arrived more than twice the frame interval apart (the camera
or the network dropped them).

The clip's queue ran full, since its body is read slower than the
camera sends, and frames were dropped up to the next keyframe; or a
pre-roll GOP larger than the window's byte cap was cut short.

The clip fell behind the stream's frames and missed some; it goes

`pairing/create`: a one-time pairing code for the control TLS

by the configuration or enrolled by pairing.

The client certificate's SHA-256, 64 hex digits, optionally with a

orientation.description:
How the picture is turned for display. A change reaches the open
sessions too, from their next frame and without a new answer.
Changing only this never reconnects.

preload.description:
Keep the source connected without viewers: connected at put and
reconnected after failures while set, so the first viewer gets a
frame from the warm GOP cache. Changing only this never reconnects;
turning it off with no viewers starts the linger.

preroll_ms.description:
Keep the last `preroll_ms` milliseconds of the stream's media in
memory, so a `clip/start` can begin before it was asked for; 0, the
default, keeps none. At most `limits.preroll_max_ms`, and each track
holds at most `limits.preroll_bytes` of whole GOPs, so the window
held may be shorter (`stream/get` reports it). Not a reason to
connect: the window fills only while `preload` or a viewer keeps
the source connected. Changing only this never reconnects.

sources.description: The sources, in order; the first that provides a kind wins.

oneOf.title: StreamPutCommand

Free it only if this session holds it when the worker handles the
release, checked atomically against a claim, so a viewer that
stops talking never frees the backchannel another session claimed

left out with an `audio_omitted` warning. `false` makes a

The upstream connection behind a source: the stream's own, since a
source URL belongs to one stream (`source_in_use`).

connected.description: A control connection authenticated with this pin is open.

fixed.description:
The pin comes from the configuration (`--control-clients`), which
`clients/remove` cannot change; otherwise it was enrolled by pairing.

pin.description:
The SHA-256 of the client's certificate, as lowercase hex pairs
joined by colons.

DeclineReason.description:
Why an offer's talk-back was declined: the `reason` of a
`backchannel_declined` warning.

oneOf.description:
The stream has no backchannel the session can feed: its source
protocol cannot carry audio back, no stream on its connection opted
in to it, the camera offers none, or it takes a codec talk-back
cannot produce from what the offer lists. Or the offer asks for
talk-back on its `sendrecv` downlink audio m-line while the
stream's audio codec cannot reach the camera, so no codec on that
m-line goes both ways (RFC 3264 §6.1): it is answered `sendonly`,
and an offer with a `sendonly` m-line for talk-back gets it. The
message says which.

Another session holds the backchannel; `backchannel/release`, its
re-offer dropping talk-back, or its close frees it.

The camera refused the backchannel for this session; `status`
carries its status code when it gave one.

The supervisor's demux counters: what the receive thread did with each

addresses_moved.description:
Learned addresses moved to another session by a verified STUN
request naming it: away from the session that held one at most

also counts as learned.

relay_discarded.description:
Datagrams from a TURN server discarded: not on a held channel, not
from a permitted peer, or neither STUN nor `ChannelData`.

relayed.description: Datagrams a TURN server relayed from a peer, unwrapped and routed.

unroutable.description: Datagrams from unknown addresses that were not a usable STUN request.

worker_full.description: Datagrams dropped because the worker's channel was full.

The longest clip, in milliseconds: the most `after_ms` may ask, and
where an open-ended clip ends (`max_duration`).

The longest pre-roll window `stream/put` may ask for
(`preroll_ms`), and so the furthest back a clip can start; 0 when
the daemon keeps none.

sessions.description: Open viewer sessions on all connections.

workers.description: The running workers, by connection id (`c1`).

Orientation.description:
`stream/put`'s `orientation`: how the picture is turned for display,
one of eight transforms by its lowercase name. Their numbers, 1 to 8,
follow the EXIF orientation tag's values, but 6 turns the picture a
quarter counterclockwise and 8 a quarter clockwise. A session
whose browser offered the video orientation extension carries it to
the browser, which turns the picture; others get it as the camera
sends it.

oneOf.description: 1: as the camera sends it.
2: mirrored left to right.
3: turned half way round.
4: flipped top to bottom.
5: turned a quarter counterclockwise, then flipped top to bottom.
6: turned a quarter counterclockwise.
7: turned a quarter clockwise, then flipped top to bottom.
8: turned a quarter clockwise.

code.description:
The code to paste into the client, `LOTSE1-<server pin>-<secret>`:
the SHA-256 of the daemon's certificate and a 128-bit secret, each
as lowercase hex. A secret: show it to the user, never log it.

expires_in_ms.description: How long the code stays valid, in milliseconds.

Pong.description: The answer to `ping`, sent instead of a `result`.

oneOf.description: The only value.
The only value.

SandboxInfo.description:
The hardening layers of the supervisor, so a client can warn the user
when one is missing.

notes.description: Why layers are missing, for humans.

Session.description: A session as `session/get` and `session/list` return it.

backchannel.description:
Talk-back towards the camera's backchannel; `false` and null when
the last answer did not negotiate it, and the counters zero until
one of the session's answers does.

dtls.description: The DTLS state, as the browser names it.

ice.description: The ICE state, as the browser names it.

orphaned.description:
No control connection owns it; it closes when the grace expires
unless a `session/adopt` takes it back.

since.description: When the offer arrived, RFC 3339 UTC.

SessionBackchannel.description:
A session's talk-back, as `session/get` reports it.
The counters are the worker's, pushed once per second, so they may lag
by that much; `negotiated`, `codec` and `talker` are current. They add
up over the session's life and never go back: a re-offer that drops
talk-back keeps them, and one that adds it again counts on.

bytes_sent.description:
Payload bytes handed to the camera's backchannel, after the reverse
transcode.

codec.description:
The talk-back codec the answer named first on that m-line, which the
browser sends (`opus`, `pcmu`, `pcma`); null when not negotiated.

negotiated.description:
The answer accepted the browser's talk-back m-line (`recvonly`, or
`sendrecv` on its downlink audio m-line).

packets_dropped_busy.description:
Of those, the ones dropped because the session did not hold the
backchannel: its offer was declined, or it was released since.

packets_received.description: Talk-back RTP packets the session received and took.

talker.description:
The session holds the camera's backchannel now: its offer claimed
it, and it keeps it until it closes, re-offers without talk-back
or `backchannel/release`.

SessionEvent.description:
An event of `webrtc/offer` and `session/adopt`, in the order 04 lists
them; `closed` is always the last.
Each variant's schema title names the Python client's class for it.

oneOf.description: The first event: the session's id, the client's or a generated ULID.
oneOf.title: SessionEventSession

oneOf.description: The SDP answer, before any candidate.
oneOf.title: SessionEventAnswer

sdp_mid.description: The media section it belongs to.

oneOf.title: SessionEventCandidate

oneOf.description: ICE or DTLS changed; also the first event of `session/adopt`.

dtls.description: The DTLS state, as the browser names it.

ice.description: The ICE state, as the browser names it.

oneOf.title: SessionEventState

oneOf.description:
Non-fatal. Each code comes at most once per session, but `backchannel_declined`, which
comes once per offer (`webrtc/offer` or `webrtc/renegotiate`) that
asked for talk-back the session did not get: the talk-back m-line
was answered `inactive` (or `sendonly` when it carries the
stream's audio too, RFC 3264 §6.1), and `reason` says why.

reason.description: Why, for `backchannel_declined`; absent for every other code.

status.description:
The camera's status code for `refused`, when it gave one
(an RTSP status, 453 Not Enough Bandwidth or 503 Service
Unavailable when a camera's one backchannel is taken by
another client); absent otherwise.

oneOf.title: SessionEventWarning

oneOf.description:
The last event; the subscription ends with it. A session still
waiting for its answer has no deadline of its own: it waits while
its source connects, and closes with the source's error as soon as
the attempt fails, at once when the offer reaches a source that has
already failed. A live source that drops is retried, at once or
after a delay, and the session waits for the retry; only a retry
that fails closes it. While a `stream/put` switches the stream to
another source, the old source's failures do not count. An answered
session rides every reconnect instead. A talk-back request the
stream cannot serve never closes a session: its answer declines
it (`backchannel_declined`).

code.description:
The stable code. Before the answer, a failed source closes the
session with its error's code, the one `stream/get` reports as
`last_error`: `source_unreachable`, `source_auth_failed`,
`source_timeout`, `source_protocol_error`, `source_ended` or
`worker_crashed`.

message.description:
For humans; for a source's error, its text as `last_error`
carries it, never the source's credentials.

oneOf.title: SessionEventClosed

sessions.description: Every session on every connection, by id.

Shutdown.description: Sent once when the daemon shuts down gracefully, before the close.

oneOf.description: The only value.

SourceBackchannel.description:
A source's backchannel as `stream/get` reports it: the camera's reverse
audio path (an RTSP camera's ONVIF backchannel, ONVIF Streaming
Specification §5.3), one per connection.

codec.description:
The codec the camera takes (`pcmu`, `pcma`, `opus`); a viewer's
talk-back in another codec is transcoded to it.

backchannel.description:
The camera's backchannel, as the connection's probe found it, while
the connection is live: what a microphone button is gated on. The
probe asks the camera on a connection of its own each time the
connection connects; nothing is opened until a talker claims it.
Null when the probe found none (the camera has none, refused the
question or could not be asked), when no stream on the connection
opted in (an RTSP source's `backchannel` option, off by default,
which turns the probe on and off without restarting the
connection), and while the connection is not live.

url.description:
The URL redacted to its origin, `scheme://[****@]host[:port]`, then
`/****` when the path is anything but empty or `/` and `?****` when
a query is present: the path and query can carry secrets (a camera
key, a session token) as the userinfo can.

options.description:
Per-scheme options, typed by the scheme's factory; unknown fields
there are rejected too.

url.description:
The source URL, credentials included; redacted everywhere it is
reported.

Stream.description: A stream, as `stream/get` returns it and `stream/list` lists it.

backchannel.description: Who talks to the camera through its backchannel.

last_error.description: The last error, if the stream is not live.

preload.description: Whether the stream stays connected without viewers.

preroll_ms.description:
The pre-roll window `stream/put` asked for, in milliseconds; 0
without one. What each track holds is its `preroll`.

since.description: When the current state began, RFC 3339.

StreamBackchannel.description:
The talker of a stream's backchannel, as `stream/get` reports it.
A camera has one backchannel, held by its source connection, so streams
that share the connection report the same talker.

since.description:
When `talker` last changed, RFC 3339; null while no offer has
claimed it since the connection's worker started.

talker.description: The session holding the backchannel, or null when it is free.

The talker of the stream's backchannel changed. Sent to the
subscribers of every stream on the source connection, never
coalesced or shed: a client too slow to take one is disconnected
(close code 1008) and reads the talker again from `stream/get`. A

The worker crashed; the crash-backoff timer runs.

av_sync_lost.description:
Times the skew watchdog withdrew the stream's audio for sync; at
most 1, since it stays withdrawn while the source runs.

clip_bytes.description: Bytes of clip files written to their bodies.

clips_completed.description:
Clips that ended with their whole file written: `completed`,
`stopped` or `max_duration`.

datagrams_rejected.description:
Datagrams refused before they were read (RTSP over UDP): from an
address other than the camera's media ports, not RTP, or from
another synchronization source.

frames_over_browser_limit.description:
Video frames the live path carried in more RTP packets than some
libwebrtc receivers assemble (2047), depending on their version;
every session sends them whole, and those viewers may freeze until
a keyframe that fits.

packets_lost.description:
RTP packets from the camera that never arrived, by their sequence
numbers: loss on the network (RTSP over UDP) or packets the camera
dropped itself.

packets_out_of_order.description:
RTP packets from the camera dropped because they came again or
after a later one (RTSP over UDP): duplicates and reordering.

Success_for_AnyValue.description: A successful `result`: exactly one per command.

Success_for_BackchannelReleaseResult.description: A successful `result`: exactly one per command.

Success_for_ClientList.description: A successful `result`: exactly one per command.

Success_for_ClipStartResult.description: A successful `result`: exactly one per command.

Success_for_Empty.description: A successful `result`: exactly one per command.

Success_for_InfoResult.description: A successful `result`: exactly one per command.

Success_for_Metrics.description: A successful `result`: exactly one per command.

Success_for_PairingCreateResult.description: A successful `result`: exactly one per command.

Success_for_Session.description: A successful `result`: exactly one per command.

Success_for_SessionList.description: A successful `result`: exactly one per command.

Success_for_Stream.description: A successful `result`: exactly one per command.

Success_for_StreamList.description: A successful `result`: exactly one per command.

Success_for_StreamPutResult.description: A successful `result`: exactly one per command.

Success_for_WebrtcRenegotiateResult.description: A successful `result`: exactly one per command.

demux.description: The demux, when the WebRTC UDP socket is open.

pss_bytes.description:
Proportional set size (`Pss` of `smaps_rollup`): the shared text
pages divided among the processes mapping them, so the figures of
all processes add up.

tasks.description:
Tokio tasks alive in its runtime; `None` until a worker's first
counters arrive.

TalkerReason.description: Why a stream's talker changed: the `reason` of `talker_changed`.

oneOf.description:
A session's offer (`webrtc/offer` or `webrtc/renegotiate`) asked
for talk-back while nobody held the backchannel; it holds it now.
The talker's session closed; the backchannel is free.

`backchannel/release` freed it; the next offer that asks for
talk-back claims it.

The talker's re-offer (`webrtc/renegotiate`) dropped talk-back;
the backchannel is free.

The camera refused the talker's backchannel session, the session
did not open in time, or its connection was lost while the talker
held it: the backchannel is free, and the talker's session got a
`backchannel_declined` warning with reason `refused`.

No stream on the talker's connection asks for the camera's
backchannel any more (the last one that did was put without the
RTSP option `backchannel`): the camera's backchannel session is
closed and the backchannel is no longer offered.

audio_delay_ms.description:
The delay a derived track's transcoder adds, in milliseconds; absent
on native tracks.

channels.description:
An audio track's channel count: 1 for G.711 and G.722 (RFC 3551
§4.5), the stream's own for Opus and AAC. Absent where
`sample_rate` is.

derived_from.description: The native track a derived track came from.

height.description: A video track's picture height in pixels, present with `width`.

preroll.description:
What the track's pre-roll ring holds for clips; null without a
window (`stream/put`'s `preroll_ms` 0). The worker's figures,
pushed once per second.

profile_level_id.description:
An H.264 track's `profile-level-id` (RFC 6184 §8.1): its sequence
parameter set's `profile_idc`, constraint flags and `level_idc` as
six lowercase hex digits, as an SDP `fmtp` spells them (`42e01f`).
Absent on other codecs, and until the camera sent its SPS.

sample_rate.description:
An audio track's sampling rate in Hz, which is not always its RTP
clock rate: G.722 samples at 16000 on an 8000 clock (RFC 3551
§4.5.2), Opus is decoded at 48000 (RFC 7587 §4.1), AAC at its
`AudioSpecificConfig`'s rate (ISO/IEC 14496-3 §1.6.2.1). Absent on
video tracks and on codecs the daemon cannot carry.

sync.description:
How the track is timed now: `arrival` until the camera's first
Sender Report for it, `sender_reports` from then on, `arrival` again
on a new timeline until the next report; at most a second old. A
derived track's is its source's.

width.description:
A video track's picture width in pixels, cropping applied (ISO/IEC
14496-10 §7.4.2.1.1, ITU-T H.265 §7.4.3.2.1). Absent on audio and
MJPEG tracks, and until the camera sent its SPS.

TrackPreroll.description:
A track's pre-roll ring, as `stream/get` reports it: whole GOPs of the
newest media, kept for clips while the stream has a window.

bytes.description:
The memory the ring holds: its frames' payloads plus a fixed cost
per frame, at most `limits.preroll_bytes`. The open GOP is also in
the track's GOP cache, so the two overlap; the frames are shared,
not copied.

held_ms.description:
The window it holds, in milliseconds: from its oldest keyframe to
its newest frame; shorter than `preroll_ms` while it fills, after
a reconnect, or when `limits.preroll_bytes` caps it.

truncations.description:
GOPs larger than `limits.preroll_bytes` the ring could keep only
the start of.

WarningCode.description:
The code of a `warning` event: every code a session may warn with,
and nothing else.

oneOf.description: Audio omitted from the session; the rest of it continues.
A `turns:` entry of `ice_servers` was ignored.
Audio withdrawn because sync could not be held.
The browser did not offer the stream's H.264 profile.
A `webrtc/candidate` the session could not parse was ignored.

A video frame needed more RTP packets than some libwebrtc receivers
assemble; it was sent whole.

The offer asked for talk-back the session did not get; `reason`
says why.

sdp.description: The SDP answer to the re-offer.

pss_bytes.description: Its proportional set size, read by the supervisor.

WorkerMetrics.description: One worker process: the one running a source connection.

pss_bytes.description:
Proportional set size (`Pss` of `smaps_rollup`): the shared text
pages divided among the processes mapping them, so the figures of
all processes add up.

relay_unbound.description: Datagrams from a relay candidate dropped for want of a channel.

restarts.description: Crash restarts of the connection's worker so far.

send_failures.description: Datagrams its sessions could not send.

streams.description: The streams reading from its connection.

tasks.description:
Tokio tasks alive in its runtime; `None` until a worker's first
counters arrive.
